Images: United States Army personnel conducted live fire exercises with the M142 HIMARS MLRS launchers during the Joint Exercise Balikatan 2026.

Like the Navy Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction Systems or NMESIS platforms of the United States Marine Corps, the M142 HIMARS also come as a common sight during the exercise, whereby the personnel belonging to the Armed Forces of the Philippines getting exposed to its operations, firepower capability, and its mobility.

The M142 HIMARS MLRS is seen as one of the candidates of the Philippine Army's MLRS Acquisition Project.

IN PHOTOS: The Gabriela National Alliance of Women stormed the Department of Finance (DOF) on the eve of Labor Day to protest the Marcos Jr. administration's insistence on maintaining the 12% Value-Added Tax (VAT) on gasoline and basic necessities. The group identified Executive Secretary Ralph Recto—a former DOF Secretary—as the chief architect of this regressive policy. The protesters also threw paint at Recto's portrait as a symbol of their anger. 

📸: Norman Cruz

IN PHOTOS: Artists apply the finishing touches to a protest effigy for Labor Day titled “Trio Delubyo” and a mural titled “Pandaigdigang Pakikibaka, Dudurog sa Imperyalista,” depicting the workers' struggle against imperialism, state violence, and economic crisis during an open house held in Quezon City on Thursday, April 30, 2026. 

The effigy, featuring US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fused into a lizard-like entity, signifies the decaying state of imperialism and its attempts to maintain global dominance, while rockets embedded in its body depict the United States’ continued war amid its waning influence in West Asia. 

📸:  Manny Palmero

data.text:
Manila Police District Director PBGen. Arnold C. Santiago issues directives to personnel during a briefing on April 30 in Manila.

More than 15,000 police officers from the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) will be deployed across Metro Manila in preparation for Labor Day on May 1. The heightened security aims to maintain public order amid anticipated rallies and protest actions in key areas of the National Capital Region.

Authorities said maximum tolerance will be observed while closely monitoring traditional protest sites. 

📸: Mark Balmores/MB

Every morning, in markets across Latin America, Southeast Asia, and Africa, millions of small transactions settle on TRON. A freelancer in Lagos receives $47 for a logo design. A family in Manila sends $82 to relatives in the province. A small business in São Paulo pays a supplier $156 for inventory. None of them care about block times, consensus mechanisms, or total value locked. They care that the money arrived in seconds, for fractions of a cent, without a bank telling them "no."

These are the transactions that power TRON's $2 trillion quarterly transfer volume. They are overwhelmingly small: 60–74% of USDT transfers are under $1,000, concentrated during daytime hours across Asia and the Americas. This is not whale activity or speculative trading; this is the global informal economy, settling on-chain, every single day. The network now hosts $86.7 billion in USDT, more than half of all USDT in circulation.

Behind these transfers is an infrastructure that has become so reliable it's invisible. Block times of three seconds. Fees measured in fractions of a cent. A resource model that separates transaction costs from token price volatility. In Q1 2026, when Bitcoin fell 24% and global crypto markets shed 20% of their value, TRX rose 9%. The network generated $82.2 million in protocol fees, second only to Hyperliquid. Usage didn't contract; it grew.

The world's largest stablecoin settlement layer didn't become that by accident. TRON was purpose-built for exactly this: high-throughput, low-cost, always-on value transfer. The 378 million accounts, the 13.8 billion transactions, the $86.7 billion in USDT these are not vanity metrics. They are the accumulated weight of millions of small decisions, every single day, by people who found a rail that works when nothing else did. The settlement layer the world actually uses doesn't need to be exciting. It just needs to work. 🔻
